It overturns `C-HISTORICAL-ASSERTION-REVIEW-4-5D40885D`'s choice to keep unrelated-archive detection as informational review notices under the later current-only policy, answering its counterweight with active-plan refusal and strict selected current-close validation rather than weaker current checks. All pre-existing archive bytes and identities are preserved and proven beyond a tracked diff; `README.md` moves only its measured footprint row and directly necessary explanation; `examples/` is unchanged.

Phase before status. The strict validator applies only to a bundle the caller explicitly selected and that is resolved under `.ngrace/changes/archive/`. It classifies the directory phase before it reads parsed status: a missing or unparseable spec, or a present non-applied status, must not escape through the existing `isAppliedArchiveBundle` early return. Both the selected spec and the selected plan must be `status="applied"`, root at the registered types (`NgraceChangeSpec`, `NgraceChangePlan`), and carry exactly one wrapper equal to the selected directory/`--change` identity. Active and pre-archive verdicts keep `CloseEvidence` inertness and are not subjected to archive-only applied requirements.

Reuse plus a narrow evidence guard. The strict validator calls the exported `validateChangeArtifact` (selected spec and plan, `location="archive"`, with `projectRoot`) and `validateSpecPlanCoverage` (selected spec to selected plan), and adds a narrow selected-close guard implemented inside `src/gates/ledger.ts` and tested in `src/gates/core.test.ts`. The guard requires every explicit `CloseEvidence` declaration in the selected `AcceptanceCriteria` to have the current consumable binding: exactly one direct `CloseEvidence` block on its bound `AC-*`, containing at least one non-empty direct `Command`. An explicit declaration that is nonbinding or unconsumable — a `CloseEvidence` under a legacy `<Criterion>` or nested below the bound `AC-*`, or more than one direct `CloseEvidence` block on one `AC-*`, or a block with no complete direct command — is refused before evaluation rather than treated as absent evidence. Ordinary `AC-*` criteria with no `CloseEvidence`, and meaningful legacy/free-text criteria with no evidence, are preserved. The grammar is not broadened, no historical schema is evaluated, no whole-project validator is called, no unrelated bundle is enumerated, and no historical reader or schema-version dispatch is introduced.

Refusal threshold. The strict validator refuses any error-severity issue from the selected spec, selected plan, selected spec-to-plan coverage, or the evidence-consumption guard. The existing warning families remain advisory and no new gate-verdict warning output is introduced; a warning-only otherwise-valid shape stays admissible unless the binding guard rejects explicit unconsumable evidence. An explicit empty or Command-less `CloseEvidence` remains the authoring error `change.close-evidence-incomplete` and is distinct from a criterion that genuinely carries no `CloseEvidence`, which is a legitimate zero-command close.

Evaluation semantics and snapshot. All bound criteria are evaluated; within one criterion execution stops on its first non-zero command and records that `Exit` and `Result`, then the remaining criteria continue. Per-criterion `Result`/`Exit` records beside any `Finding`/`Ack` children; a `pass` is refused when any selected command fails, and a legitimate `outcome=fail` records the failed-command evaluations. The existing stale-location, directory-identity, spec-byte, and ledger-byte guards are preserved, and the decision-bearing snapshot adds the selected `plan.xml` bytes. The snapshot guarantee is limited to those decision-bearing spec/plan/ledger/directory bytes; the `.ngrace-lint.json` read used only to classify command shapes is not part of the decision snapshot, because a warning does not decide the verdict.

C-REVIEW-CURRENT-BOUNDARY-1-217D3F0D.Problem:
The current-only policy in `AGENTS.md` and the withdrawn compatibility campaign in `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/grace-implementation-queue.md:154-156` withdraws historical archive compatibility: older archive contents are passive LLM evidence, not current operational inputs. The first slice, `C-CURRENT-VALIDATION-BOUNDARY-1-D8D7DF85`, made the automatic grammar, lint, and query paths current-only and explicitly deferred the review, selected-close, and teaching consumers. Two defects and two teaching errors remain in the current product, and the selected-close counterweight is incomplete.
First, `src/review/core.ts:508-567` globally discovers `changes/**/plan.xml`, parses archived contents, and emits `review.historical-path-absent` from archived `MustExist` values; `runReview` invokes that global detector before the selected audits (`:1561-1590`). An unrelated archived plan is thereby a current review input. Measured 2026-10-06 on this repository at base `c58e93f2e6f6a91b8bf5528edd3b29724652390c`: `ngrace review --path . --severity info` reports exactly three `review.historical-path-absent` infos, and archived path mutation changes review output while exact restoration reproduces it. Discover active plans before any content read; remove the obsolete archive-notice producer and guide; preserve active `MustExist` refusal, including Baseline and undeclared/unexempt Target claims, and preserve the other current project detectors and selected audits. The intentional read of an explicitly selected archived current-close record by its own consumer is not the removed global read.
Second, `src/gates/ledger.ts:437-584` can record a selected current-close `pass` with a malformed or missing spec, a wrong root or wrapper identity, missing criteria, an incomplete or unconsumable `CloseEvidence`, a non-applied status, or a missing/malformed/mismatched plan. The evaluator `evaluateCloseEvidenceChildren` (`:546-584`) returns an empty child list when the spec is missing, is not applied/archive, has no `C-*` wrapper, or fails to parse, and `recordReviewVerdict` then records `pass` because no child records `Result=fail` — shape, value, and skipped-evidence failure silently become zero evidence. The existing `isAppliedArchiveBundle` early return lets a missing/invalid spec or a present non-applied status escape validation. Measured across two synthetic consumers via the real CLI: malformed/missing/wrong-identity selected inputs and archived non-applied statuses recorded `pass` exit 0 with a ledger write and exact restoration restored valid evaluation; a Command mutating the selected plan bytes during evaluation also recorded `pass`; a legacy `Criterion` with explicit failing evidence and two direct evidence blocks each passed with the command skipped or only the first block run while the exported validators reported no issues, and nested evidence passed with a `change.acceptance-criterion-unmapped` coverage warning rather than a refusal. The strict selected validator must refuse these rather than record them, while preserving the existing guards.
Third, `ngrace-plan` rule 6 (`SKILL.md:62`) presents this repository's flush, retirement, and live-root operations without an adopter/example qualifier, reading as universal GRACE requirements. Fourth, rule 19 (`SKILL.md:75`) says absent archived scratch `MustExist` claims produce `review.confidently-wrong`; that claim is already false and becomes plainly false once the first defect is fixed. Faithful copies should be taught to carry the actual inputs consumed by current planned verification and selected current-close commands, with scratch and VCS metadata conditional on those consumers, plan-time rehearsals distinguished from close-time verification, and the accurate active-plan refusal teaching and other verification/copy safeguards retained.
